Sergeant Catherine Tladi

By: Busisiwe Gumede | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Sergeant Tladi cried tears of joy when Sello Mapunya, a serial rapist she spent years hunting was finally locked away for the rest of his life. How did she end his reign of terror in Pretoria?

Unique Selling Point:
Sergeant Catherine Tladi worked tirelessly to put serial rapist Sello Abram Mapunya behind bars. We follow the trail of evidence she and the team investigated which finally led to his arrest.

Summary:
She is an officer who was instrumental in bringing down Abraham Sello Mapunya. Sello
is a Pretoria serial rapist who recently received one of South Africa’s harshest
sentences ( five life terms and 988 years in jail).

He began his rape and robbery spree in 2014 - terrorising areas like Mamelodi, Atteridgeville, Olievenhoutbosch and
Nelmapius, where he stayed with his girlfriend. For nearly five years he would leave her
sleeping at night, between 2am and 4am to go and rape and plunder. More than 50
victims could not identify him because they never saw his face. But he left his DNA
behind and he made the vital mistake of giving his girlfriend one of the cell phones
which he had stolen from a victim.

Sergent Catherine Tladi, a rape survivor herself,
made it her mission to stop the man in his tracks. This included having a strong
relationship with his victims and finding key evidence against him. South Africa is known
as the rape capital of the world but there are dedicated and passionate coppers like
Tladi, who start a case and see to its conclusion. What does it take to bring down a
serial rapist like him? She says you have to think like one and never forget to also fit
into the shoes of the survivors.

Further information:
Sergent Refilwe Tladi is a woman who grew up in atteridgeville. She never planned to be a police officer. In fact it was her husband who came home with a form one day and begged her to apply. He himself applied for the same position. Sergeant Tladi says she didn’t want to apply for the position because she was studying at vaal tech but had to stop her dream of being an engineer because of lack of funds. In any case, on the last day to apply for the post she signed on the dotted line and they both waited. She hates guns and still grapples with her own. What’s ironic is that she was called back for an interview and not her husband. She bagged her job and says she started out certifying documents and opening cases worked her way up from there.

She was keen to work in any division that dealt with violence against women and children. She is a survivor of a gang rape when she was 15 years old and says that she remembers how she felt afraid every single day. This was because her perpetrators were never found. This made her extremely suicidal. She has tried to commit suicide five times. She says she found a home in the SA police. She trained in CSC and was eventually recruited to the detective unit. She worked in Garsfontein for a while and eventually joined the Serial Electronic Crime Investigations...

This is a small unit that focuses on nabbing serial killers and rapists. They analyse data, interview people in communities and gather evidence to get people like Sello Mapunya. A serial rapist who recently received one of South Africa’s harshest sentences (five life terms and 988 years in jail).

This story will give us a view of what happens at the Serial Electronic Crime Unit - this is a devision tasked with solving one of South Africa’s major problems - rape. Not many people know about their work and we have full access to them for the day. We will start the day early with them and basically shadow them on an operation. This will help us visually tell the story better.

Press Release:


He was a man who spent five years terrorising women of all ages from Pretoria's East to western suburbs. Now serial rapist Sello Mapunya is serving over a thousand years in prison. Heading the team of investigators on the high-profile case Sergeant Catherine Tladi of the Gauteng Serial Electronic Crime Investigations (SECI) paid a high personal price to become the hero that’s now changing the world one conviction at a time. Carte Blanche meets the incredible officer who used tragedy in her own life to restore women’s lives.

Producer: Busisiwe Gumede-Chizhanje | Presenter: Masa Kekana

Script:


VO – For years, gender based violence has
ravaged South African communities.
Most concerning are sexual offences – more than
50 000 cases of rape, sexual assaults and
attempted sexual assaults were reported between
April 2019 and March 2020. Many more are
brushed under the carpet.

The police department tasked with solving these
crimes is the Family Violence, Child Protection
and Sexual Offences Unit - or FCS. Sgt. Catherine
Tladi is a proud member of this outfit.
UPSOUND – SGT. CATHERINE TLADI (CLIP
003.MXF)
MASA - 06:45 - what attracted you to the unit?
TLADI – 06:54 – … I was once a victim of a gang
rape. 09:02 – I didn't have any help. No one took me
through the pain of rape. 08:52 – I tried to kill myself
three times so for me it was that I don't want
someone dying out of this.
VO – That was many years before she joined the
force and she was too scared to report the
incident.
UPSOUND – SGT. CATHERINE TLADI
07:02 – I want to be an answer that I never got to
have in my time of need.
VO - After studying trends in stats relating to
sexual crimes, in 2018, FCS established a
specialised investigative division called the Serial
Offenders and Electronic Crimes Unit, SECU.
These sleuths focus specifically on crimes
committed by the same culprit as well as
electronic crimes, particularly - child
pornography.

MASA LINK – In October 2018, SECU investigators
began looking into a string of attacks on women in
townships around Pretoria – not knowing that the
case would be of historic significance.
NATSOUND - ANNELIE MOIMA
00:15 Our father, who art in heaven...
Three years ago, Annelie Moima worked late
shifts. She often got to her Atteridgeville home in
the west of Pretoria just before midnight – with
only enough time to say her prayers and sneak
quietly into bed next to her son.
On the 28 th of January in 2018, after her nightly
devotion, a nightmare would unfold...
UPSOUND – ANNELIE MOIMA
05:07 - ... I just saw someone with a phone lighting
my face and he said “can you please move, move
move move!!!”,
VO – The intruder pushed Annelie into another
room where her twin sister and nephew were
sleeping.
UPSOUND – ANNELIE MOIMA
06:39 - He covered us with a blanket so that we can’t
recognise him. When my twin sisters son was
peeping, he was like I’m going to shoot that child.
VO – He pulled the blanket over their faces.
UPSOUND – ANNELIE MOIMA
05:26 - ... he was like … remove your pants … and
did whatever he wanted to do with me. And the sad
part of it is that he was very much comfortable.
VO – The intruder raped Annelie and would do so
repeatedly over the two hours that followed – in
front of her family. During this time, he ate from the fridge the fridge and robbed the family of their money
and cellphones.

UPSOUND – ANNELIE MOIMA
07:56 - ... He came back again for the third time and
he kissed my ass and said okay I’m done. Thank you
my love. And he left. I was devastated.
VO - When this case was reported to SECU, the
Modus Operandi sounded familiar to Tladi.

UPSOUND – SGT. CATHERINE TLADI
MASA19:34 What was his modus operandi
…a lot of women.
The same, go through the window, torch you
rape you , it’s either if at all others are fast
asleep and you’re not making noice . He
would rape you there they’ll be surprised
whe. They see you aiming and you say
someone was here and they raped me
VO – In 2018, another woman was at the mercy of
the serial rapist when he struck in Nellmapius.
28 year old Naledi Rentini was sleeping with her
child when she woke up to a large man, pressing
a gun to her throat.
UPSOUND – NALEDI RENTINI

04:56 - … He requested money and phones then I
gave him. 05:13 and then he requested me to lay flat
on my bed and then he said I should cover my head
with a blanket and then from there that’s when he
raped me.
VO – She was also violated repeatedly.

UPSOUND – NALEDI RENTINI
08:15 - After this happened, I went to live with my
granny, because I was afraid of living here. … I
couldn’t sleep.
MASA LINK – To unmask the thieving rapist, police
first had to interview his victims, among them a girl
who was fourteen at the time of the assault.
VO – Tladi and her partner, Sergeant Moloantwa
Raphagadi drove around Pretoria trying to find
the women who had reported these crimes.
UPSOUND – SGT. CATHERINE TLADI
02:27 - … the hardest job was getting all 56 victims,
notifying them and getting further statements, going
to check on the places, the scene of crimes, where
this whole thing happened, some relocated, some no
longer using the phones they gave at the time of the incident.
VO – Compiling an identikit of the suspect was
also a challenge because he always instructed
his victims to cover their faces.
But police caught a break...
Stealing his victim's phones would be his
undoing. Using mobile device tracking
technology, police linked one of the stolen
phones to the suspect's girlfriend.

UPSOUND – SGT. CATHERINE TLADI
22:07 - The girlfriend said ehh this phone I was given
by my boyfriend. “Where is your boyfriend?”. Now
they traced the boyfriend. When they got him, they
took them both, she had to give a statement to say I
was offered the phone
VO – DNA collected from the victims' rape kits
matched the suspect now in custody.
Finally, police had the name of the serial rapist –
Sello Abram Mapunya.
MASA LINK – Sello Mapunya initially pleaded not
guilty to an array of charges including rape,
housebreaking and robbery. But when the state piled
on the pressure, meticulously presenting indisputable
evidence gathered by SECRU, he changed his plea
to guilty.
VO – In May this year, before sentencing the
convicted rapist, Judge Papi Mosopa noted that
Sello was “not the type of person willing to live
side by side with others in peace” and that he
was “hell bent on encroaching the dignity of
others.”
Masopa then sentenced Sello to five life terms
plus 988 years behind bars. All in all, Sello's
crimes earned him 1088 years in jail.
SOUND UP - CATHERINE TLADI SPEAKS
OUTSIDE OF COURT.
01:26 - ... All the effort that went into this case paid
off. I’m happy for my victims more than anything.
VO – With Sello in jail for the rest of his life, at
least two of his victims say they can now sleep
through the night.
UPSOUND – ANNELIE MOIMA

18:00 I’m finally at peace. Now I can take my
happiness back from Sello because he took my
happiness now I’m taking it back.

UPSOUND – NALEDI RENTINI
11:09 - ... I was very happy especially seeing him
being sentenced - the look on his face, I see that he
can now feel the same pain that I felt.
VO – And this is why Sergeant Tladi is intent on
solving every case that lands on her desk - to
give victims the closure they deserve so they can
heal and rebuild their shattered lives.
UPSOUND – SGT. CATHERINE TLADI
41:24 - If you have never been through this you’ll
never understand when someone tells you, “the day
they raped me, they took a coat off me. And I’ve been
naked since. When you find justice. It’s like they put it
back. It’s like they cover you again.

A serial rapist who recently received one of South Africa’s harshest sentences (five life terms and 988 years in jail). This story will give us a view of what happens at the Serial Electronic Crime Unit - this is a devision tasked with solving one of South Africa’s major problems - rape. Not many people know about their work and we have full access to them for the day. We will start the day early with them and basically shadow them on an operation. This will help us visually tell the story better.
